title: A guess that aims the search
hook: Add a guess of the steps left, and the search stops spreading in every direction.

knows: cheapest-first search settles cells in order of cost so far (cheapest-is-not-shortest)
a search that spreads out in rings (wave-from-the-corner)
doesNotKnow: that a guess of the distance left can focus the search
that an honest underestimate keeps the shortest-route guarantee

misconception: To find the shortest route you have to spread out in every direction until you hit the goal.
objective: The learner can explain that ranking cells by steps so far plus a guess of steps left, where the guess never overestimates, settles far fewer cells (7 instead of 31 on the open grid) and still finds a shortest route.

claims.text: On an open 7 x 7 grid with 4-way moves, start in the middle of the left edge and goal in the middle of the right edge, ranking cells by steps so far plus Manhattan steps left settles 7 cells, goal included, and finds a 6-step route. With no guess, 31 cells are settled and the route is also 6 steps. Ties go to the cell with more steps taken, then to the cell added first.
claims.source: Builder's node script (same algorithm and tie-break as Demo.tsx): start (col 0, row 3), goal (col 6, row 3), goal counted when settled; guess 7 settled / route 6, no guess 31 / route 6. The spec reports the same 7 and 31 under three other tie-breaks (fewer steps taken, first-in-first-out), so the open-grid numbers do not depend on the rule. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own node re-implementation (fc1/astar.mjs) with the Demo.tsx rule (score, then more steps taken, then first added; goal counted when settled): open grid guess 7 settled / route 6 (settle order (0,3)..(6,3)), no guess 31 / route 6. Also 7 and 31 under fewer-steps-first, FIFO and LIFO. Source-text nit (not learner-facing): it says 'three other tie-breaks' but names two.

claims.text: With a 3-cell wall (column 3, rows 2 to 4), the guided search settles 16 cells and finds a 10-step route; with no guess all 46 open cells are settled and the route is also 10 steps. The 16 depends on the tie-break (more steps taken first): first-in-first-out gives 32.
claims.source: Builder's node script (same algorithm and tie-break as Demo.tsx): guess + wall 16 / route 10; no guess + wall 46 / route 10. The spec's note gives 32 for first-in-first-out. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Same script: wall col 3 rows 2-4, guess 16 / route 10, no guess 46 / route 10 (49 - 3 walls = 46 open). FIFO and fewer-steps-first give 32, LIFO 20, so the 16 is tie-break dependent, as the claim says. Route 10 = 6 across + 2 out + 2 back.

claims.text: A* with a guess that never overestimates the steps left finds a shortest route.
claims.source: Hart, Nilsson & Raphael (1968), A formal basis for the heuristic determination of minimum cost paths, IEEE Trans. Systems Science and Cybernetics 4(2): optimality with an admissible heuristic. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Hart, Nilsson & Raphael, IEEE Trans. SSC 4(2):100-107, July 1968 (DOI 10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136, confirmed by web search): admissible heuristic gives a minimum-cost path. Manhattan on this grid is also consistent, so the stage's no-reopen version is optimal too.

claims.text: On a grid with 4-way moves, the count of columns plus rows between a cell and the goal never overestimates the steps left.
claims.source: Each step changes the column or the row by at most 1, so any route needs at least |dc| + |dr| steps. Walls can only add steps. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: each 4-way move changes |dc| + |dr| by exactly 1, so any route needs at least |dc| + |dr| moves; walls only remove moves.

claims.text: The guess ranks cells nearer the goal first, so the search runs at the goal instead of flooding every direction.
claims.source: On the open grid every cell on row 3 has score 6 (steps so far + steps left) and every other cell scores at least 8, so the search settles row 3 first. Seen on the stage as numbers 1 to 7 along one row. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: a cell (c,r) has g >= c + |r-3| and h = (6-c) + |r-3|, so f >= 6 + 2|r-3|: row 3 scores 6, every other cell >= 8. Node settle order is exactly the 7 row-3 cells, numbered 1 to 7 on the stage.

recall.question: A search ranks cells by steps so far plus a guess of steps left. When does the guess keep the route found a shortest one?
options: When it never says more steps are left than there really are
When it is exactly right for every cell
When it is always bigger than the real distance
recall.why: A guess that never overestimates cannot push a cell on a shortest route behind a worse one. A guess that is too big can.
